info.title: Paddock HTTP API
info.description:
HTTP API for Paddock — the keeper-agent platform (persistent chats, projects, unified triggers).

This document is **generated from the server's route schemas** via `@fastify/swagger`, so it
tracks the code: a new or changed route with a schema shows up here automatically.

**Live chat is WebSocket, not REST.** Sending a message, streaming the response, tool-call
events, cancel, slash-commands and the live queue all flow over `GET /ws`. This spec covers the
HTTP surface: reads, project/chat/trigger/git management, instance config, and attachment
upload/serve. The two-step attachment flow is: `POST .../chats/:sessionId/upload` (HTTP, here)
then reference the returned file ids in the `chat:send` WebSocket frame.

## Authentication

Paddock has no built-in login — authentication is provider-agnostic and handled at the edge (reverse proxy / IdP). **When these docs are served by the Paddock instance itself, behind your proxy, a `Try it out` request is a same-origin call that inherits your existing SSO session — it authenticates automatically, nothing to paste here.** Use the **Authorize** button only for the explicit-token path (a different origin, a programmatic client, or testing without the proxy).

This instance runs **jwt** mode: a signed token in the `Authorization` header, verified against the JWKS.

bearerAuth.description: JWT auth (`PADDOCK_AUTH_MODE=jwt`). A signed token verified against the configured JWKS (`PADDOCK_AUTH_JWKS_URL`), sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

get.description: Reports whether voice dictation is enabled on this instance so the composer can decide whether to show a mic button. Returns a JSON object with `available` (boolean), `mode`, and `model`.

200.description: Transcription capability info.

schema.description: Transcription capability info.

post.summary: Transcribe a recorded audio blob
post.description: Accepts `multipart/form-data` with a single `file` field (a recorded WebM/Opus audio blob) and runs whisper (remote OpenAI-compatible endpoint or local whisper.cpp). Returns a JSON object with `text`, `model`, `mode`, and `durationMs`. Returns 503 when dictation is disabled, 400 when no file is present, and 413 on oversize/malformed uploads.

200.description: Transcription result.

schema.description: Transcription result.

get.description: Returns the authenticated principal for this request. In `none` auth mode this is the frozen anonymous principal (`{ username: "anonymous", anonymous: true }`); in trusted-header / jwt modes it is the real proxy/IdP identity. Returns a JSON object describing the user.

200.description: The request principal.

schema.description: The request principal.

get.description: Liveness probe. Returns a JSON object `{ ok: true }`.

200.description: Service is up.

schema.description: Service is up.

get.description: Reports every surfaced instance-config field (value / default / editable / sensitive / env-shadow) for the top-level admin screen. Returns a JSON object keyed by field.

200.description: Instance config snapshot.

schema.description: Instance config snapshot.

put.description: Writes the editable subset of the instance config to paddock.config.yaml (comment-preserving, atomic). Writes DO NOT hot-apply — the config is frozen at boot — so a successful write returns `{ restartRequired: true, configPath }` and the process keeps its current config until it restarts. Returns 400 on a malformed patch or invalid field, 500 on write failure.

patch.description: Map of config field name to new value to write.

200.description: Write accepted; restart required to apply.

schema.description: Write accepted; restart required to apply.

get.description: Returns the models this instance offers (the built-in catalog filtered to the `PADDOCK_MODELS` / YAML `models:` allow-list; unset ⇒ the whole catalog) plus the keeper/sweeper defaults and the box-wide defaults (drive mode, max spawn depth, recovery, attachments, curation) that projects fall back to when their own overrides are unset. `keeperDefault` is the effective default for the offered list. Returns a JSON object with `models`, `keeperDefault`, `sweeperDefault`, `keeperDriveModeDefault`, `maxSpawnDepthDefault`, `recoveryDefault`, `attachmentsDefault`, and `curationDefault`.

200.description: Model list and inherited defaults.

schema.description: Model list and inherited defaults.

get.description: Lists the scratch agent's slash commands (the one-off-chat equivalent of the per-project commands endpoint). Returns a JSON object with `commands`; on failure returns 503 with `{ commands: [], error }`.

200.description: Available scratch-chat slash commands.

schema.description: Available scratch-chat slash commands.

get.description: Returns the herdctl fleet status and the list of agents. Returns a JSON object with `status` and `agents`; on failure returns `{ status: null, agents: [], error }`.

200.description: Fleet status and agent list.

schema.description: Fleet status and agent list.

get.description: Serves the raw file bytes of an attachment addressed by its opaque id (a file the agent shared via send_file, or a composer upload). Returns the raw bytes with `Accept-Ranges: bytes` — a `Range` request is honored with `206 Partial Content`, otherwise the full body with `200`; `416` for an unsatisfiable range and `404` when the id is unknown. Locked down with nosniff + a sandbox CSP.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Opaque attachment id from the chat transcript.

200.description: Default Response

post.summary: Composer file upload
post.description: Accepts `multipart/form-data` with one or more `file` fields; copies each posted file's bytes into the attachment store and returns opaque ids the composer holds until send. Validation is server-authoritative (enabled/size/count/type per the effective project config). Returns a JSON object with `files` (each `{ id, filename, size, kind }`). Returns 403 when attachments are disabled, 413 on oversize/too-many files, 415 on a disallowed type, and 400 when no files are present.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Chat session id; accepted for a not-yet-created chat too (it only scopes the request).

200.description: Stored attachment descriptors.

schema.description: Stored attachment descriptors.

get.summary: Get fleet-level git remote and GitHub connection state
get.description: Returns the configured backing-store remote details merged with a `github` object describing the current GitHub device-flow connection status.

200.description: Object containing the remote configuration fields plus a nested `github` object with connection state.

schema.description: Object containing the remote configuration fields plus a nested `github` object with connection state.

post.summary: Push the working tree to origin
post.description: Pushes the projects working tree to the configured remote (the NAS bare repo / origin). Returns an object describing the push result.

200.description: Object describing the outcome of the push operation.

schema.description: Object describing the outcome of the push operation.

post.summary: Begin GitHub device-flow authentication
post.description: Starts the GitHub device-flow authorization and returns the device/user codes and verification URL. Responds with 400 (`{ error }`) if the flow cannot be started.

200.description: Object with the GitHub device-flow details (e.g. device code, user code, verification URI).

schema.description: Object with the GitHub device-flow details (e.g. device code, user code, verification URI).

400.description: Error object `{ error }` when the device flow cannot be started.

schema.description: Error object `{ error }` when the device flow cannot be started.

post.summary: Poll GitHub device-flow authentication
post.description: Polls GitHub for completion of a previously-started device flow using the supplied `deviceCode`. Returns the current auth status; responds with 400 (`{ error }`) if `deviceCode` is missing.

deviceCode.description: The device code returned by the connect step.

200.description: Object describing the current device-flow poll result / auth status.

schema.description: Object describing the current device-flow poll result / auth status.

400.description: Error object `{ error }` when `deviceCode` is missing.

schema.description: Error object `{ error }` when `deviceCode` is missing.

post.summary: Disconnect the GitHub connection
post.description: Clears the stored GitHub credentials / connection. Returns `{ ok: true }` on success.

200.description: Object `{ ok: true }` confirming the disconnect.

schema.description: Object `{ ok: true }` confirming the disconnect.

get.summary: Get a project's git working-tree status
get.description: Returns the uncommitted changes confined to this project's subtree. Returns `{ repo: false }` when the projects dir isn't a git working tree. Never throws on git errors.

200.description: Object describing the project's working-tree status, or `{ repo: false }` when not a git working tree.

schema.description: Object describing the project's working-tree status, or `{ repo: false }` when not a git working tree.

get.description: Returns the raw unified diff (text/plain) for the project's tracked changes (working tree vs HEAD), or for a single file via `?file=`. Untracked files are reported by /git/status instead.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: Optional project-relative path to diff a single file.

200.description: Default Response

post.summary: Commit a project's pending changes
post.description: Commits the project's pending changes. Optional `files` (project-relative) commits only those changes; omitted commits the whole subtree. Returns an object where `committed: false` indicates there was nothing to commit. Push is a separate explicit action (/api/git/push).

message.description: Optional commit message; defaults to `Update <project name>`.

files.description: Optional project-relative paths (array) to commit only those changes.

200.description: Object describing the commit result; `committed: false` when there was nothing to commit.

schema.description: Object describing the commit result; `committed: false` when there was nothing to commit.

get.description: Returns `{ projects }`, an array of project objects. Each entry carries the project metadata plus a compact `chatTurns` array (per-chat `{ sessionId, lastTurnCompletedAt, lastSeen? }` for the sidebar UNREAD count) and a `dirty` uncommitted-file count.

200.description: Object with a `projects` array; each item is a project object enriched with `chatTurns` and `dirty`.

schema.description: Object with a `projects` array; each item is a project object enriched with `chatTurns` and `dirty`.

post.summary: Create a project
post.description: Creates a project from `CreateProjectInput` and registers its keeper/sweeper agents. Set `repo` to create a repo-backed project (cloned checkout as the keeper cwd); omit it for a notebook project. Responds 201 with `{ project }`.

slug.description: URL slug (derived from name if omitted).

repo.description: External git repo URL to back this project (repo-backed if set).

schema.description: Object with the created `project`.

get.description: Returns `{ project }` for the root project (the project whose directory is the projects root), or `{ project: null }` when this instance has no root project. Existence gates the root Home/Chat UI; nothing seeds it.

200.description: Object with the root `project`, or `null`.

schema.description: Object with the root `project`, or `null`.

post.summary: Create the root project
post.description: Writes `<projectsRoot>/project.yaml` and registers the root keeper + sweeper agents. This is the opt-in that turns the instance root into an ordinary project (root Home, root chats). Responds 201 with `{ project }`, or 409 if one already exists.

name.description: Human-readable name (defaults to the root directory name).

schema.description: Object with the created root `project`.

get.description: Returns `{ project, changelog, chats }` — the project metadata, its raw CHANGELOG.md text, and its chats (sessions) enriched with archived/starred/last-seen/provenance/trigger flags. Per-chat usage rings are filled separately by the client.

200.description: Object with `project`, `changelog` text, and a `chats` array.

schema.description: Object with `project`, `changelog` text, and a `chats` array.

patch.description: Applies an `UpdateProjectInput` partial and re-registers the keeper. Keeper overrides (`model`, `permissionMode`, `maxTurns`, `docker`, `driveMode`, `maxSpawnDepth`, `hooksMcpEnabled`) are validated at runtime — an invalid value returns 400. Tri-state override fields accept `null` to clear the override. Responds with `{ project }`.

permissionMode.description: Keeper permission mode override (validated at runtime).

docker.description: Whether the keeper runs in Docker.

recovery.description: Keeper-chat recovery override object; `null` clears it.

curation.description: Sweeper-curation budget override object; `null` clears it.

200.description: Object with the updated `project`.

schema.description: Object with the updated `project`.

delete.description: Removes the project directory and unregisters its keeper + sweeper agents (the inverse of create). Responds with `{ ok: true, slug }`.

200.description: Object with `ok: true` and the deleted project `slug`.

schema.description: Object with `ok: true` and the deleted project `slug`.

post.summary: Promote a notebook project to repo-backed
post.description: Clones `repo` into the project's nested checkout, flips the keeper cwd to it, and re-registers the keeper (keeping existing chats + metadata). A missing/blank `repo` returns 400; clone failure rolls back to the intact notebook. Responds with `{ project }`.

repo.description: Git repo URL to clone and back the project with.

200.description: Object with the promoted `project`.

schema.description: Object with the promoted `project`.

get.summary: List one level of a project's file tree
get.description: Lists a single directory level. `?path=<subpath>` descends into a subdirectory (omitted/empty = project root). Returns `{ path, kind, entries }`: a directory yields `kind: "dir"` with `entries` (dirs first); a path naming a file yields `kind: "file"` with empty `entries` (200, not an error).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Subpath to descend into; omitted/empty = project root.

200.description: Object with `path`, `kind` ("dir" | "file"), and an `entries` array.

schema.description: Object with `path`, `kind` ("dir" | "file"), and an `entries` array.

get.description: Returns the raw CHANGELOG.md text with content-type `text/markdown; charset=utf-8` (empty string if none). No response schema — the body is raw markdown text, not JSON.

200.description: Default Response

get.description: Returns the raw OVERVIEW.md text (sweep-curated current-state context) with content-type `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`; empty string if the project has no overview yet. No response schema — the body is raw markdown text, not JSON.

200.description: Default Response

get.summary: List a project's keeper slash commands
get.description: Returns `{ commands }` — the slash commands available to the project's keeper agent (built-ins plus the project's `.claude/commands` and MCP-provided commands) for composer autocomplete. Result is memoized per agent.

200.description: Object with a `commands` array.

schema.description: Object with a `commands` array.

get.description: Dual-mode. By default returns JSON with the file content plus a render-kind hint (markdown | html | text | image). With `?raw=1` it instead STREAMS the file's raw bytes with the correct Content-Type (locked down: sandbox CSP + nosniff + inline disposition) — how the image viewer loads an ``. No response schema is declared so the raw byte stream is never corrupted.

parameters.name: raw
parameters.description: Set to a truthy value (e.g. `1`) to stream raw bytes instead of JSON.

200.description: Default Response

put.summary: Pin a file as a sibling tab
put.description: Pins `file` as a sibling tab (validates the file exists + dedupes). Responds with `{ project }` reflecting the updated pins.

file.description: Path of the file to pin.

200.description: Object with the updated `project`.

schema.description: Object with the updated `project`.

delete.description: Removes the pin for the given URL-encoded file `name`. Responds with `{ project }` reflecting the updated pins.

parameters.name: file
parameters.description: URL-encoded name of the pinned file to remove.

200.description: Object with the updated `project`.

schema.description: Object with the updated `project`.

get.summary: List a project's triggers plus the picker catalog
get.description: Returns the project's trigger DTOs together with the Triggers-tab picker catalog. Success (200) is an object with `triggers` (array of trigger DTOs, each combining the `trigger` when-clause, the `run` definition, `enabled`, and derived fields like `agentName`), `grantableTools` (the tools an event/webhook trigger may be granted), `events` (the lifecycle events an event trigger can fire on), and `triggerTypes` (the supported trigger kinds).

200.description: The trigger DTO list plus picker catalog (`triggers`, `grantableTools`, `events`, `triggerTypes`).

schema.description: The trigger DTO list plus picker catalog (`triggers`, `grantableTools`, `events`, `triggerTypes`).

get.description: Fetches a single trigger's config by name. Success (200) is an object with a `trigger` field holding the trigger DTO (`trigger` when-clause + `run` + `enabled` + derived fields). Returns 404 when the project declares no trigger with that name.

200.description: An object with a `trigger` field holding the trigger DTO.

schema.description: An object with a `trigger` field holding the trigger DTO.

put.description: Creates or fully replaces a trigger keyed by name, persisting it to project.yaml then arming it. Enabling/disabling is this same route with `enabled` flipped. The body is the FULL trigger record: `trigger` is the WHEN clause — a discriminated union on `trigger.type` (`schedule` with `cron` xor `interval`; `event` with an `on` value such as `onArchive`/`afterTurn`; `webhook` with a `path`, shape-reserved) — `run` is the shared agent-run definition (prompt/promptFile, model, tools, etc.), and `enabled` is the on/off flag. Success (200) is an object with a `trigger` field holding the persisted trigger DTO. Returns 400 for an invalid name or malformed trigger definition.

trigger.description: The WHEN clause: a discriminated union on `trigger.type` (`schedule`/`event`/`webhook`) with type-specific fields.

run.description: The WHAT clause: the shared agent-run definition (prompt/promptFile, model, tools, session mode, etc.).

enabled.description: Whether the trigger is armed; new triggers default disabled.

200.description: An object with a `trigger` field holding the persisted trigger DTO.

schema.description: An object with a `trigger` field holding the persisted trigger DTO.

delete.description: Removes a trigger from project.yaml AND disarms it (an event trigger's agent is torn down; a schedule trigger's forwarded entry is dropped). Success (200) is an object with `ok: true`, the `name`, and `removed` describing what was removed.

200.description: An object with `ok`, `name`, and `removed`.

schema.description: An object with `ok`, `name`, and `removed`.

get.summary: Live runtime state for a project's triggers
get.description: Per-trigger live last-run / next-run / status, joining each trigger's config with herdctl runtime state (the cron scheduler's next-fire + status for schedule triggers, plus job records for last run). This is a static path segment, matched BEFORE `/:name`, so no trigger name shadows it. It is served as its own pollable endpoint (separate from the config list). Success (200) is an object with a `runtime` field describing each trigger's live state.

200.description: An object with a `runtime` field describing each trigger's live last-run/next-run/status.

schema.description: An object with a `runtime` field describing each trigger's live last-run/next-run/status.

post.summary: Run a trigger now
post.description: Fires a trigger immediately ("Run now") through the same hub path a cron/event fire uses, producing a first-class badged run. Fires any trigger type regardless of its `enabled` flag. Success is 202 with an object containing `ok: true`, the `name`, and the started `sessionId`. Returns 503 when firing is unavailable, 404 for an unknown trigger, 409 for the post-turn curator trigger (not runnable on demand), and 502 if the fire started no chat.

202.description: An object with `ok`, `name`, and the started `sessionId`.

schema.description: An object with `ok`, `name`, and the started `sessionId`.

get.description: Returns the project's chats (sessions) with per-chat metadata (name, last-turn time, archived/starred flags, last-seen watermark, run provenance, trigger info). Usage rings are fetched separately (see GET /api/projects/:slug/chats/usage). Response: an object `{ chats: [...] }`.

200.description: Object `{ chats }` where `chats` is an array of chat DTOs.

schema.description: Object `{ chats }` where `chats` is an array of chat DTOs.

post.summary: Get the WS target for a new project chat
post.description: Thin endpoint: validates the project and returns the WebSocket target for opening a new chat. It does NOT create the chat or send a message — a new chat is minted lazily by the first WS `chat:send` (with no sessionId), and the session id arrives in `chat:complete`. Responds 201 with `{ projectSlug, sessionId: null, ws: "/ws", note }`.

201.description: Object `{ projectSlug, sessionId, ws, note }` giving the WS target `/ws`.

schema.description: Object `{ projectSlug, sessionId, ws, note }` giving the WS target `/ws`.

get.description: Returns the project's 'while you were away' run history (scheduled + spawned + human runs) sourced from herdctl job records joined with provenance markers, plus the per-user since-last-visit watermark. Response: an object describing runs and the last-seen digest state.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Max number of runs to return (clamped server-side).

200.description: Object with the project's runs and since-last-visit digest state.

schema.description: Object with the project's runs and since-last-visit digest state.

post.summary: Mark a project's runs as seen
post.description: Advances the per-user 'runs last seen' watermark (clears the since-last-visit digest). Optional body `{ when }` (epoch-ms) defaults to now; monotonic in the store (an older `when` is a no-op). Response: `{ ok, lastSeen }`.

when.description: Epoch-ms timestamp to record as last seen; defaults to now.

200.description: Object `{ ok, lastSeen }` with the recorded watermark.

schema.description: Object `{ ok, lastSeen }` with the recorded watermark.

get.summary: Bulk context-window usage for a project's chats
get.description: Returns per-chat context-window usage keyed by session id, for all of a project's chats — the expensive data the chat list needs for its usage rings. Sessions with no usage data are omitted. Response: `{ usage: { <sessionId>: <usage> } }`.

200.description: Object `{ usage }` mapping session id to its context-window usage.

schema.description: Object `{ usage }` mapping session id to its context-window usage.

get.description: READ-ONLY: returns the messages of a project chat, enriched with tool details and per-message provenance, plus a synthetic trailing notice if the chat dead-ended at a usage/subscription limit. Sending a message is WebSocket-only (a `chat:send` frame on GET /ws) — there is no HTTP send-message endpoint. Response: `{ messages: [...] }`.

200.description: Object `{ messages }` with the chat's message array.

schema.description: Object `{ messages }` with the chat's message array.

get.summary: Read a sub-agent's transcript within a project chat
get.description: Returns the step-by-step transcript of a sub-agent launched from a Task/Agent tool block within a project chat. `toolUseId` is the parent tool_use id carried on the enriched tool call. Response: `{ messages: [...] }`.

parameters.name: toolUseId
parameters.description: Parent tool_use id of the sub-agent launch.

200.description: Object `{ messages }` with the sub-agent's message array.

schema.description: Object `{ messages }` with the sub-agent's message array.

get.summary: Context-window usage for a project chat
get.description: Returns the context-window usage for a project chat, read from the transcript's most recent turn — lets the UI show 'context used' before a new turn streams a fresh value. Response: `{ usage }`, where `usage` is null when the transcript has no usage data.

200.description: Object `{ usage }` (null when the transcript has no usage data).

schema.description: Object `{ usage }` (null when the transcript has no usage data).

delete.description: Deletes a project chat (session): removes its transcript JSONL and clears any archived/starred flag so a future session id can't inherit it. Responds 200 with `{ ok, removed }`.

200.description: Object `{ ok, removed }` indicating whether the transcript was removed.

schema.description: Object `{ ok, removed }` indicating whether the transcript was removed.

patch.description: Sets or clears a project chat's custom display name. A null/empty `name` in the body clears any custom name. Responds 200 with `{ ok }`.

name.description: New display name; null/empty clears the custom name.

200.description: Object `{ ok }`.

schema.description: Object `{ ok }`.

post.summary: Fork a project chat
post.description: Eagerly duplicates a project chat's transcript into a NEW session in the same project (leaving the source untouched), so the fork exists immediately as a real, resumable chat with the parent's history. Optional body `{ name }` sets the fork's title; optional `{ fromUuid }` branches at an earlier message so the fork inherits only the prefix up to that turn (issue #451). Responds 201 with `{ sessionId }` (the new session id).

name.description: Title for the new forked chat.

fromUuid.description: Message uuid to branch at; the fork inherits only the history up to that turn. Omitted ⇒ the full transcript.

201.description: Object `{ sessionId }` with the new forked session id.

schema.description: Object `{ sessionId }` with the new forked session id.

post.summary: Revert a project chat to an earlier message
post.description: Truncates the chat's transcript at `uuid`, in place (same session id), so the conversation continues as if the later turns never happened. The dropped tail is backed up and recoverable. Rolls back the CONVERSATION only — real side-effects of the reverted turns are NOT undone. Requires body `{ uuid }` (400 without it). Returns an object with the count of removed messages.

uuid.description: Message uuid to truncate at (required; 400 when missing).

200.description: Object reporting how many messages were removed.

schema.description: Object reporting how many messages were removed.

post.summary: Archive or unarchive a project chat
post.description: Non-destructive toggle of a project chat's persisted archived flag — the transcript is untouched and the chat stays openable/resumable/forkable. Body `{ archived }` defaults to true; a real transition into archived fires the project's onArchive hooks. Responds 200 with `{ ok, archived }`.

archived.description: Target archived state; defaults to true when omitted.

200.description: Object `{ ok, archived }` with the resulting archived state.

schema.description: Object `{ ok, archived }` with the resulting archived state.

post.summary: Star or unstar a project chat
post.description: Non-destructive toggle of a project chat's persisted starred flag (orthogonal to archiving; a starred chat sorts to the top of its population). Body `{ starred }` defaults to true. Responds 200 with `{ ok, starred }`.

starred.description: Target starred state; defaults to true when omitted.

200.description: Object `{ ok, starred }` with the resulting starred state.

schema.description: Object `{ ok, starred }` with the resulting starred state.

post.summary: Mark a project chat as seen
post.description: Persists the user's last-viewed moment for a project chat server-side, driving the cross-device unread affordance. Optional body `{ when }` (epoch-ms) defaults to now; monotonic in the store (an older `when` is a no-op). Responds 200 with `{ ok, lastSeen }`.

when.description: Epoch-ms timestamp to record as last seen; defaults to now.

200.description: Object `{ ok, lastSeen }` with the recorded watermark.

schema.description: Object `{ ok, lastSeen }` with the recorded watermark.

post.summary: Mark a project chat unread
post.description: Sets (or clears) the per-user MANUAL unread override so a chat resurfaces its unread cue even after its last turn was seen — the email "mark as unread" pattern. Body `{ unread }` defaults to true; clearing it is equivalent to marking seen (see the `/seen` route). Returns `{ ok, unread }`.

unread.description: Whether to flag the chat unread. Defaults to true.

200.description: Object `{ ok, unread }` reflecting the stored flag.

schema.description: Object `{ ok, unread }` reflecting the stored flag.

get.description: Returns all one-off scratch chats with per-chat metadata (usage, archived/starred flags, last-seen watermark, run provenance). Scratch chats never get context preload. Response: `{ chats: [...] }`.

200.description: Object `{ chats }` with an array of scratch chat DTOs.

schema.description: Object `{ chats }` with an array of scratch chat DTOs.

get.description: READ-ONLY: returns the messages of a one-off (scratch) chat, enriched with tool details. Sending a message is WebSocket-only (a `chat:send` frame on GET /ws) — there is no HTTP send-message endpoint. Response: `{ messages: [...] }`.

200.description: Object `{ messages }` with the chat's message array.

schema.description: Object `{ messages }` with the chat's message array.

get.summary: Read a sub-agent's transcript within a scratch chat
get.description: Returns the step-by-step transcript of a sub-agent launched from a Task/Agent tool block within a one-off (scratch) chat. `toolUseId` is the parent tool_use id. Response: `{ messages: [...] }`.

parameters.name: toolUseId
parameters.description: Parent tool_use id of the sub-agent launch.

200.description: Object `{ messages }` with the sub-agent's message array.

schema.description: Object `{ messages }` with the sub-agent's message array.

get.summary: Context-window usage for a scratch chat
get.description: Returns the context-window usage for a one-off (scratch) chat, read from the transcript's most recent turn (see the project variant). Response: `{ usage }`, where `usage` is null when the transcript has no usage data.

200.description: Object `{ usage }` (null when the transcript has no usage data).

schema.description: Object `{ usage }` (null when the transcript has no usage data).

delete.description: Deletes a one-off (scratch) chat: removes its transcript and clears any archived/starred flag. Responds 200 with `{ ok, removed }`.

200.description: Object `{ ok, removed }` indicating whether the transcript was removed.

schema.description: Object `{ ok, removed }` indicating whether the transcript was removed.

post.description: Persists the user's last-viewed moment for a one-off (scratch) chat (same as the project variant). Optional body `{ when }` (epoch-ms) defaults to now; monotonic in the store. Responds 200 with `{ ok, lastSeen }`.

post.summary: Promote a scratch chat into a new project
post.description: Promotes a one-off (scratch) chat into a NEW project: creates the project + keeper, then re-homes the chat's transcript into it so it lists and resumes under the project. `name` is required (validated at runtime; a missing/blank name returns 400). Responds 201 with `{ project, promoted, sessionId }` — `promoted:false` means the project was created but the transcript couldn't be moved (e.g. an unknown session id); the project is still usable.

name.description: New project name (required; validated at runtime).
